initial_reasons.AGNES: She watches the hawk with quiet familiarity, alert to the unfamiliar man approaching but not yet inviting his attention.
initial_reasons.WILL: He tries to appear composed while looking for a natural reason to remain near her.

AGNES.reason: She turns her attention from the hawk to acknowledge the stranger with measured courtesy.
Her question is direct but guarded as she studies what has brought him to Hewlands.
Recognizing him as the Latin tutor, she quietly reassesses the unfamiliar man.
She presses him for an explanation, curious about his presence in the garden.
She lightly challenges his awkwardness, keeping her attention on him without becoming openly hostile.
His mention of the bird draws her attention back to the hawk, the safer subject between them.
She corrects him with restrained amusement, making clear that the distinction matters to her.

WILL.reason: His hesitation exposes his uncertainty, and he briefly looks away while searching for an answer.
The broken explanation makes him visibly uncomfortable as he struggles to frame his real motive.
He searches for a plausible excuse, momentarily looking inward as he assembles the words.
Another hesitation betrays how self-conscious he feels under her scrutiny.
He shifts his attention to the hawk, relieved to have found a less personal subject.
